issues.description: Indentation bug: `if sys.version_info` block sits outside the class but the registration decorator is meant to wrap `Math_unary`
issues.detail: In mathdecl.py the new block `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11): Math_unary = infer_global(math.exp2)(Math_unary)` is placed immediately after the class body with a blank line removed. The logic is correct, but the prior blank line separating the class from the next `@infer_global(math.atan2)` was deleted, harming readability of an already subtle decorator-as-function call. State the invariant in a comment: `Math_unary` is reused as a registry target for each unary signature.

issues.description: Missing `import sys` in numba/cpython/mathimpl.py and numba/np/math/mathimpl.py despite using `sys.version_info`
issues.detail: Both files gain a `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):` guard but the diff shows no `import sys` added. If `sys` is not already imported at module top, this raises NameError at import time on Python < 3.11 (and even on 3.11+). The audit must verify the import exists; otherwise the guard itself is broken. A correct guard that fails to import is worse than no guard.

issues.description: Version guard is unnecessary and adds conditional surface area; numba should declare its minimum Python
issues.detail: `math.exp2` exists since Python 3.9, not 3.11. The guard `>= (3, 11)` is both incorrect about the introduction version and likely unnecessary if numba's supported minimum is already >= 3.9. Choose the right invariant: either drop the guard entirely (preferred — fewer code paths to reason about) or set it to the actual introduction version. Conditional registration is a maintenance tax that should be justified.

issues.description: Release note file missing trailing newline
issues.detail: `docs/upcoming_changes/10276.new_feature.rst` ends with `\ No newline at end of file`. POSIX text files end with a newline; many tools (towncrier, RST parsers, git diff) behave better with one. Trivial fix, but the kind of thing a careful reader notices.

issues.description: Test inputs duplicate `-2` and omit zero and negative fractional values
issues.detail: `x_values = [-2, -1, -2, 2, 1, 2, .1, .2]` repeats `-2`/`2` and never tests `0.0` or negative floats. For `exp2`, `exp2(0)=1` is a useful invariant check, and negative fractional inputs exercise the LLVM intrinsic differently. This was copied from `test_exp`; the pattern is propagating. State the property under test rather than mimic.

issues.description: No literate comment explains why `Math_unary` is re-decorated post-definition
issues.detail: A reader encountering `Math_unary = infer_global(math.exp2)(Math_unary)` must reverse-engineer that `infer_global` is a decorator factory being called as a function to register an additional global against the same template class. One sentence — `# Register math.exp2 against the existing unary template; added post-class because it is conditional on Python version.` — would save every future reader the same five minutes.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED with a likely import bug. The functional approach — reusing `Math_unary` as the typing template and binding `llvm.exp2` for the implementation — is correct and parsimonious; this is the right way to add a unary math intrinsic. However, the version guard targets the wrong Python version (`math.exp2` arrived in 3.9, not 3.11), and the two `mathimpl.py` files use `sys.version_info` without an obvious `import sys` in the diff context — that must be verified or the guard fails at import. The code is also NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT: the post-class `infer_global(math.exp2)(Math_unary)` pattern deserves one sentence of explanation, and the test inputs were copy-pasted with a duplicate and no zero/negative-fraction coverage. Small, fixable, mergeable once the import and version guard are corrected.
